output: Hypothesis: In the context of the World Bank dataset, increased education spending (measured as adjusted savings for education expenditure as a percentage of GNI) has a positive impact on per capita GDP (measured as GNI per capita in constant 2015 US dollars) in Lower Middle Income Countries (LMC). However, the analysis revealed a negative coefficient of approximately -635.07, suggesting that increased education spending is associated with a decrease in per capita GDP in this group. This result contradicts the hypothesis, indicating that the relationship between education spending and GDP may not be positive in LMC countries. Due to missing data, a comprehensive analysis for Sub-Saharan Africa could not be performed.
